area.title: Notification hub (overview task list)
area.scope: The notification hub: its heading, status strip, commodity total cards, the numbered task list sections and rows, which rows show for which commodity, row statuses and what makes each complete, the Review and submit and Return to dashboard buttons. Stops at the pages the rows open and at the review page.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. It sets how the rest are weighed: the prototype wins by default over what the real services do today; only a DR1 judgement on the same difference, or a real constraint the prototype cannot express (persistence, validation, authentication, cross-service behaviour), overrides it.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.
